department: Neuroscience Graduate Program (MD Anderson UTHealth Houston GSBS)

deadline.value: Students apply through GSBS Biomedical Sciences Ph.D. umbrella admissions; Fall 2027 international deadline is November 1, 2026 (domestic final deadline December 1, 2026).

also.quote: Applications for Fall 2027 for the PhD programs (Biomedical Sciences and Medical Physics) and SMS programs (Genetic Counseling and Medical Physics) are now available!

gre_subject.value: No ETS GRE Subject Test exists for neuroscience (ETS offers only Mathematics, Physics, and Psychology), and GSBS does not consider GRE scores.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE is neither required nor recommended as part of the application. GRE scores are not taken into consideration by the Admissions Committee when reviewing an application.

also.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Students enter through GSBS umbrella admissions and complete three tutorial rotations before selecting a faculty advisor and affiliating with the Neuroscience Graduate Program.
supervisor.quote: Students are admitted directly to the graduate school through an umbrella admissions process and not into departments or programs. Entering PhD students perform three tutorial rotations before selecting a faculty advisor and joining a graduate program.

funding.value: All admitted GSBS PhD students receive a Graduate Research Assistantship (GRA) with a $41,500 annual stipend (effective Fall 2026), full tuition and required fees payment, and health insurance benefits.
funding.quote: Graduate Research Assistantships (GRA) are provided to all PhD students. These assistantships require no service other than degree-related academic activities and include:

also.quote: Payment of the student’s tuition and required fees

entry_route.value: A bachelor's degree or higher is required for PhD admission.

notes: Dedicated GSBS Neuroscience Ph.D. program offering a Fast Track option (starting Molecular & Cellular Neuroscience in Fall) or Traditional Track alongside three first-year rotations.
